structured_output.statement: Example 3.23 (Section 3.4, p. 156): given a 37.2% (by mass) HCl aqueous solution of density 1.19 g/mL, find the mass of HCl contained in 0.500 L of the solution.
structured_output.notes:
This is a mass-percentage / solution-concentration computation (volume → mass via density, then mass percent → solute mass). It is neither chemistry.molar-conversion (no moles, no molar mass, no atomic masses are involved or printed) nor chemistry.mass-balance (no chemical equation with reactants and products). Per rule 4 it must not be bent into the nearest registered type.

Two further points, recorded but not decisive since rule 4 already disqualifies the passage: (a) the worked example's own numeric result is not readable — the text layer carries the set-up sentence and the flowchart/equation caption but not the computed value; the only figure in the Solution's discussion is the rough estimate "about 200 g" ("5 40 = 200 g"), which the passage itself labels an estimate, not the result. (b) "282 mL" after Answer: belongs to the Check Your Learning question (what volume contains 125 g of HCl?), a different question from the worked example's givens, so per rule 2 it must not be attached to those givens.

No atomic masses are printed anywhere in the passage.
